evidence: deepseek uses `if idx == n` and `for c in range(1, 4)`; gpt-oss states `order is fixed 0..n-1 for lexicographic minimality`; glm states `Since n <= 40, we use meet-in-the-middle`
affordance_in_statement: The system delivers power to $n$ separate industrial complexes ... ($1 \le n \le 40$) ... every complex must be assigned to one of the three networks
removal_suggestion: There is no compliant removal: all survivors exploit the immutable n <= 40 bound together with the three-coloring structure. Rephrasing the scenario would not remove that affordance, while changing the bound or number of networks is prohibited.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses meet-in-the-middle over two halves, made feasible by the maximum of 40 vertices and three colors

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: It attempts all 3^n assignments in lexicographic order, so worst-case instances time out despite the n <= 40 limit.

recommended_edit: No legal single edit can defeat all survivors: doing so would require changing the immutable size bound or the three-network task structure. The explicit worst-case warning is not an enabling shortcut and removing it would not reliably defeat these solutions.
